label: D1 late in episode (trial>=75) after an a2->S2 common transition (stay-on-a2)
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO/D2), only late in the episode (no activity before trial ~70; rate rises from trial 70-79 to 90-99, and so does magnitude). Within that window it fires when the previous trial was a2 reaching S2 by a common transition, and the agent goes on to choose a2 again (99% of mass has upcoming action a2; choice logit moderately negative, value low). Prior reward 1 carries 80% of mass but is not required. The second clause (prev_action unknown & upcoming action a2) only covers the window first trial, where the previous trial is outside the window; it uses the agent own upcoming choice (legitimate). The observed-only predicate D1 & ep_trial>=75 & prev_action==2 & prev_common==1 scores dev F1 0.816 (P 0.85, R 0.79), losing mostly those boundary steps. Does not fire after a1 choices or after rare transitions (prev_common 0: 0.1% rate), nor early in episodes.

issues: Minor: the onset at trial 75 is a soft ramp, not a step. With the observed-only clause (D1 & prev a2 common), precision by episode band on dev is 0.05 at trials 70-74, 0.50 at 75-79, 0.90 at 80-89 and 0.97 at 90+. Trials 90+ carry 55% of the activation mass. So 'trial>=75' slightly overstates how reliably it fires right at 75. Moving the cutoff to 77 only changes test F1 from 0.877 to 0.894, so this is a threshold tweak, not a missing class.

Minor: 'stay-on-a2' is mostly but not strictly true. After an a2-common trial late in the episode, the feature still fires on 32% of D1 steps where the upcoming choice is a1. That is 1.6% of activations and 0.7% of activation mass, so it is negligible.

The window-boundary clause (prev_action==-1 & action==2) has precision 0.67 on dev. It uses the upcoming choice as a stand-in for a previous trial that falls outside the window. That is a data limitation, and the explanation states it openly.

All checked claims hold. D1 only: GO and D2 have 0 active steps. Nothing fires before trial 70: ep_trial<70 gives 0 hits. After a1 the rate is about 0.03%. After a2-rare: precision 0.000. After a1-rare: 0.015. Upcoming a2 carries 99.2% of the mass, and prev_reward 1 carries 80%. Test misses are 707 steps holding 0.4% of the mass, which is scattered noise. False positives are concentrated at the trials 75-79 ramp.

Observed-only check: D1 & ep_trial>=75 & prev_action==2 & prev_common==1 scores test F1 0.811 (P 0.838, R 0.786). The gap to the recorded predicate comes only from the window's first trial, as the explanation says. Since prev_action==2 & prev_common==1 is the same as prev_state==2 given that a1 never reached S2 here, the feature is effectively 'late-episode D1 after the agent reached S2 via a2'.
